perspective:
From Ethan Mohamud’s available perspective:

- Ethan is a plumber; Gary Guo is a doctor and a close friend since middle school. They have relied on each other for emotional and professional support.
- Ethan noticed Gary working excessively long hospital hours, skipping meals, and sacrificing sleep. He became concerned about Gary’s health.
- Ethan invited Gary to a two-day weekend retreat to relax and regain perspective.
- Gary initially refused, saying he appreciated Ethan’s concern but could not go because there was too much to do at the hospital.
- Ethan attended the retreat with Gary. There, Ethan observed Gary acting restless and avoiding discussions about work, leading Ethan to suspect there was more to Gary’s overworking than professional obligations.
- Ethan told Gary they had been friends since middle school, that Gary could tell him anything, and that Ethan was there to help, not judge.
- Gary told Ethan it was complicated and that he didn’t want to burden him.
- Gary then opened up to Ethan about the pressures of managing a new department and personal challenges he was facing.
- Ethan suggested prioritizing tasks and delegating some responsibilities. Gary agreed and said he could use help organizing his schedule to make time for himself.
- Over the following months, Ethan regularly checked in with Gary, discussed his progress and challenges, and offered support and encouragement.
- Gary told Ethan things were better, that he was less overwhelmed thanks to Ethan’s help, and that he had had time for a movie.
- After about a year, Ethan saw Gary as capable of managing a healthier balance on his own. Ethan decided to step back but remain available.
- Ethan told Gary he was always just a call away. Gary thanked him, said he couldn’t have done it without Ethan’s support, and said he felt more in control.
